question: Can one minimal generic capability model distinguish optional amortized acquisition from mandatory feasibility acquisition, allow capabilities with no validated fallback, and preserve explicit not-ready/outside-evidence decisions, while simultaneously preserving all 114,688 first-family decisions and satisfying the frozen P8 bounded oracle?
minimal_semantic_delta: Capability has a required preferred primitive and an optional validated fallback primitive.
Evidence profile reuse metric is optional.
Acquisition paths distinguish REUSE_AMORTIZED from MANDATORY_FOR_FEASIBILITY.
MANDATORY_FOR_FEASIBILITY paths are forbidden from carrying reuse thresholds.
NOT_READY is a first-class no-route result.
OUTSIDE_VALIDATED_CAPABILITY is a first-class evidence-boundary result.

claim_boundary.established: One minimal generic semantic model covers both (1) optional reuse-amortized represented primitives with a validated fallback and (2) mandatory feasibility-enabling represented primitives with no validated fallback.
claim_boundary.not_established: Universality across all future primitive families.
claim_boundary.p8_boundary: P8-G remains FAIL and full inference remains unauthorized.

next_scientific_step.question: Can the frozen v2 capability/acquisition semantics represent an independently validated direct-execution primitive family such as closed I002, whose preferred execution primitive requires neither a new resident representation nor an acquisition action, without abusing residency state, inventing acquisition/lifetime semantics, or changing the v2 registry/policy core?
